# <span class="en">Introduction and study context</span><span class="zh">引言与研究背景</span> {#sec-intro}

::: {.en}
Rail transit shapes a city as much as it serves one. In Singapore the MRT has linked new
towns to jobs since 1987, and it is the backbone of a land-scarce, high-density plan.
Building it is also a wager on future demand. A station's structure has to go in when the
line is built, years before anyone can know how many people will live around it.

The wager has not always paid promptly. Buangkok and Woodleigh were complete when the
North East Line opened in June 2003, and both stayed closed for lack of development around
them. Buangkok opened in January 2006 and Woodleigh in June 2011
[@wiki_buangkok; @wiki_woodleigh]. Hume, on the Downtown Line, was left as a structural
shell because projected ridership did not justify finishing it, and it opened only in
February 2025 [@wiki_hume]. These are not stories of bad planning. Building a shell
early is cheap against building it later, and running an empty station is expensive.
What the decision needs is a defensible estimate of how many people a station would
serve and from where, and a clear statement of how sure that estimate is.

By 2030 two more projects will test the same judgement. The Jurong Region Line opens in
stages from 2028 with 24 stations by 2029 [@lta_jrl]. Cross Island Line Phase 1 follows
in 2030 with 12 [@lta_crl]. Together they reach Tengah, Jurong West, Nanyang Technological
University and the industrial west, and connect Pasir Ris, Hougang and Ang Mo Kio without
passing through the city.

Probabilistic spatial interaction models were built for this kind of question. The Huff
model treats a place as a choice among competing destinations, with the probability of each
rising with its attractiveness and falling with distance [@huff1963]. It has since been
applied well beyond retail, to park-and-ride catchments [@lin2016], hospital service areas
[@bai2023], store closures [@bahrami2022] and rail station catchments [@zhu2021]. The last
of these is closest to the present work, and differs in one way that shapes this report. Zhu
et al. adopt a distance exponent of 2 and weight station attractiveness by expert opinion,
rather than calibrating attractiveness against observed ridership. Singapore publishes tap-ins
for every station in every hour, so here the model can be calibrated and, more usefully, tested.
:::

::: {.zh}
轨道交通既服务城市，也塑造城市。自 1987 年以来，新加坡地铁把新市镇与就业中心连接起来，是这座土地稀缺、
高密度城市规划的骨干。但修建地铁也是对未来需求的一场押注：车站结构必须在建线时一并完成，而那时距离
人们入住周边还有很多年，谁也无法确知会有多少人住在那里。

这场押注并不总能及时兑现。东北线 2003 年 6 月开通时，Buangkok 与 Woodleigh 均已建成，却因周边缺乏
开发而继续关闭。Buangkok 于 2006 年 1 月开放，Woodleigh 则迟至 2011 年 6 月
[@wiki_buangkok; @wiki_woodleigh]。滨海市区线的 Hume 因预测客流不足而只留下结构外壳，到 2025 年
2 月才开放 [@wiki_hume]。这些并非规划失误的故事：提前留好结构比日后再建便宜，而运营一座空车站却很昂贵。
这类决策需要的是：对车站将服务多少人、这些人来自何处的站得住脚的估计，以及清楚说明这个估计有多可靠。

到 2030 年，又有两个项目将考验同样的判断。裕廊区域线自 2028 年起分阶段开通，到 2029 年共 24 个车站
[@lta_jrl]；跨岛线第一期随后于 2030 年开通，共 12 个车站 [@lta_crl]。它们将通达登加、裕廊西、南洋理工
大学与西部工业区，并在不经过市区的情况下连接巴西立、后港与宏茂桥。

概率空间交互模型正是为这类问题而生。Huff 模型把一个地点视为对多个竞争目的地的选择，选择每个目的地的概率
随吸引力上升、随距离下降 [@huff1963]。它早已超出零售领域，被应用于停车换乘的集散范围 [@lin2016]、医院
服务区 [@bai2023]、门店关闭决策 [@bahrami2022] 以及轨道车站的集散范围 [@zhu2021]。最后这项研究与本文
最接近，但有一处差别决定了本报告的走向：Zhu 等人采用 2 作为距离指数，并以专家意见为车站吸引力加权，而不是
依据观测客流校准吸引力。新加坡公布了每个车站每小时的进站量，因此这里的模型可以校准，更重要的是可以检验。
:::

## <span class="en">Research questions and objectives</span><span class="zh">研究问题与目标</span>

::: {.rq .en}
*RQ1 · Calibrate.* How well can a probabilistic spatial interaction model reproduce
ridership at Singapore's stations, including stations it was not calibrated on, and what
makes a station attractive once distance and competition are accounted for?
:::

::: {.rq .zh}
*研究问题一 · 校准。* 概率空间交互模型能在多大程度上复现新加坡各车站的客流，包括未参与校准的车站？在考虑
距离与竞争之后，是什么让一个车站具有吸引力？
:::

::: {.rq .en}
*RQ2 · Predict.* What ridership can the proposed Jurong Region Line and Cross Island Line
Phase 1 stations expect, how uncertain is it, and which of them risk being the next
station too quiet to justify opening?
:::

::: {.rq .zh}
*研究问题二 · 预测。* 拟建的裕廊区域线与跨岛线第一期车站可望有多少客流？不确定性有多大？其中哪些有可能成为
下一个因太冷清而难以开放的车站？
:::

::: {.rq .en}
*RQ3 · Impact.* How would the proposed stations change the ridership and market areas of
stations already open, and how far from the new lines does the effect reach?
:::

::: {.rq .zh}
*研究问题三 · 影响。* 拟建车站将如何改变既有车站的客流与市场区？这种影响能从新线延伸到多远？
:::

::: {.en}
The value-added analysis in @sec-va asks two further questions the core model cannot
answer: how many of the new stations' riders would be new to rail, and where they go once
through the gate.
:::

::: {.zh}
@sec-va 的附加价值分析进一步提出核心模型无法回答的两个问题：新站的乘客中有多少是轨道交通的新用户，以及
他们进站之后去向何处。
:::
